name: apple-pages-mcp
description: Read, create and export Apple Pages documents through the Pages app
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Pages app on this Mac.

Pages has no framework a separate process can use, so this server drives Pages itself through Apple events — the same route apple-notes-mcp takes for Notes. Pages must be running, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation. The app may show as "Pages Creator Studio" there and in permission dialogs; that is a display-name change Apple made, not a different app.

Pages has no library the way Notes has folders — it only knows about documents open right now. documents_list shows what is open; open_document opens a file that is not.

Every result is bounded. document_get returns the body one window at a time, or the text of a range of pages, and documents_list returns one page of documents; when a result does not hold everything, its first lines say how much there is and the exact arguments that return the rest (character_offset and max_characters, first_page and last_page, limit and offset). A size, an offset or a page number outside its range is moved to the nearest allowed value, and the result says which one was used. A call that has not finished after 60 seconds is abandoned and answered with an error that says so; a write already sent to Pages may still take effect.

update_document makes you say whether you are appending or replacing. Silently replacing a whole document's body is the mistake worth designing against.

create_document and update_document (replace mode) accept styled paragraphs — real headings and quotes, via font/size/color, the entire scriptable surface Pages exposes for a paragraph. Tables, shapes, images and charts cannot be created at all through Pages' scripting interface, confirmed live.

Password-protected documents are refused by every tool that would read, write or export one, and no tool accepts a password as an argument — the same policy apple-pdf-mcp uses for encrypted PDFs.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: pages_status
tools.description: Reports whether Pages is running, whether this server may automate it, and the sizes and deadline in force. Touches no document.

tools.name: documents_list
tools.description: Lists the documents open in Pages, one page at a time in name order, with page count and whether each has unsaved changes; limit and offset reach the rest.

tools.name: document_get
tools.description: Returns one open document's page/section/table/image/chart counts, whether it is password protected, and its body as plain text one window at a time (character_offset, max_characters), or the text of a range of pages (first_page, last_page).

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Creates a new, unsaved document in Pages — optionally from a named template, with an initial body as plain text or as styled paragraphs (headings, quotes).

tools.name: open_document
tools.description: Opens the Pages document at 'path' and returns its name, path, page count and id. Its text is read with document_get.

tools.name: update_document
tools.description: Changes an open document's body. 'mode' is REQUIRED and decides whether text is appended or the whole body is replaced. Replace accepts styled paragraphs (headings, quotes) as an alternative to plain text.

tools.name: save_document
tools.description: Saves an open document, to its existing path or to a new one. Requires confirm=true when the destination already exists.

tools.name: close_document
tools.description: Closes an open document. Defaults to discarding unsaved changes; saving requires confirm=true.

tools.name: export_document
tools.description: Exports an open document to pdf, word, epub, rtf, plain_text or pages09. Requires confirm=true when the destination already exists.
